text: Very slow reimbursement. We have had Figo for more than five years. For the first four years, Figo was fantastic. Claims were paid within 3-4 days. If a claim was denied, you could appeal the decision and they would try and work with you. I recommended Figo to everyone. Over the course of the past year, that has ALL changed. My dog was diagnosed with malignant melanoma. Every 3 months she goes to the same Oncologist for the same immunotherapy shot and x-ray. I file the same paperwork with SOAP notes and for the same amount. For the past 5 years this has been consistent. What has changed is the length of time before they pay the claim. It has gone from days to weeks before we get reimbursed. What is most frustrating is that I am on autopay so I pay THEIR bill the day it is due but then wait WEEKS for them to pay me. I have addressed this with Figo multiple times but it never changes. I filed the exact same claim July 10 but it is August 1 — a full 3 weeks and Figo finally approved the claim today. I still haven’t received the money but the claim has been closed. Sadly, I am getting to the point that I can no longer recommend Figo.

Trial Subscription Cannot be Cancelled. I signed for a free cloud trial for 7 days and now want to cancel.  

However the app does not a have an easy way to cancel  as the trial subscription does not appear in my Apple subscriptions nor anywhere on the app. The company likely is doing this intentionally to extract dollars from those that don’t have 60 minutes going over every menu in the app to find out how to cancel the subscription. 

By the way here is the long procedure, which is not intuitive at all, to cancel the trial subscription: 1)click on bottom right icon labeled “Me”; 2) click feedback; 3) click manage subscription 4) click on weblink Petlibro.app; 5) login with your user name and password; 6) click on the icon that looks like a person; 7) click on billing history; 8) and finally click stop auto-renew. YIKES.  This took me over an hour to find since it is not intuitive at all. Those that paid for the subscription would appreciate a law firm to file a class action lawsuit against Petlibro.
